description: A general guide to help you prepare for your move to Canada.

items.text: Research and compare Canadian cities (cost of living, weather, jobs, etc.)
Check visa or immigration requirements
Prepare important documents (passport, medical records, pet papers, etc.)
Save emergency funds (at least 3–6 months of expenses)
Book your flight(s)
Research pet travel requirements (if applicable)
Cancel or transfer current utilities and subscriptions
Notify your bank and set up international access
Research rental areas and average prices
Shortlist neighbourhoods near transit and work or school
Contact real estate agents or browse trusted rental websites
Prepare rental documents (proof of income, references, credit score)
Schedule viewings (virtual or in person)
Sign a lease and pay deposits
Set up renter’s insurance
Get a Canadian SIM card
Apply for a Social Insurance Number (SIN)
Open a Canadian bank account
Apply for provincial health insurance (e.g. OHIP in Ontario)
Register with a family doctor or walk-in clinic
Get a local transit card (e.g. Presto, Compass, OPUS)
Update your address with all institutions
Explore nearby grocery stores and pharmacies
Get household essentials and furniture
Set up internet and utilities
Meet your neighbours and explore the community
Learn recycling and waste rules in your area
Find your nearest public library or community centre
Update your resume to Canadian standards
Apply for jobs or attend networking events
Understand taxes and register with the CRA (Canada Revenue Agency)
Set up online banking and budgeting tools
Learn about Canadian credit scores
Join local expat or newcomer groups
Attend cultural or community events
Explore parks, cafes, and attractions
Learn basic French if moving to Quebec
Try local food specialties
Register your pet with a local vet
Get updated vaccinations and pet insurance
Learn pet bylaws (leash, noise, etc.)
Find pet-friendly parks and pet stores
